answer: The evidence partially supports the hypothesis: 72 of 256 universes show a statistically significant positive association, while none show a statistically significant negative association. However, 184 universes are indeterminate, and inference changes substantially across some outcome, exposure-model, adjustment, and skin-tone-encoding choices, so the broad claim is not uniformly established.
rationale: Positive significant results outnumber contrary significant results (72 versus 0), and all 256 estimates have confidence intervals, but the large indeterminate share and high inference-flip rates prevent robust support. The evidence also mixes distinct outcome definitions and treatment contrasts rather than testing one identical dark-versus-light claim throughout.
key_evidence: 72 of 256 universes have significant positive effects; 0 have significant negative effects.
184 of 256 universes are classified as indeterminate, although no universes are unavailable and all 256 have confidence intervals.
Inference flip rates are 51.56% for straight-red-only versus all-sendings-off outcomes and 31.08% for fixed-covariate adjustment choices.
Median standardized effects differ across adjustment choices, from 0.000059 for player-characteristics/referee-bias adjustment to 1.201 unadjusted; exposure-model medians range from 0.508 to 1.579.],
refinement_reason: The multiverse combines different red-card outcomes, event/exposure estimands, and skin-tone representations. These choices define substantively different claims, especially because some specifications use continuous or multi-level skin-tone predictors rather than a direct dark-versus-light contrast.
refinement_dimensions: Outcome definition: all sendings-off versus straight red cards only
Event/exposure estimand: count rate, any-event probability, versus exposure-adjusted event rate
Skin-tone measurement and encoding: binary dark-versus-light versus continuous or five-level representations
suggested_hypotheses: Referees are more likely to award any sending-off, including second-yellow sendings-off, to dark-skinned than to light-skinned players under a prespecified binary skin-tone contrast.
Referees are more likely to award straight red cards to dark-skinned than to light-skinned players under a prespecified binary skin-tone contrast.
The rate of sending-offs per game is higher for dark-skinned than for light-skinned players under a prespecified exposure-adjusted count model.
caveats: The supplied summary does not report the number or distribution of non-significant results separately from the 184 indeterminate results.
Standardized effects from different outcome and exposure models are not necessarily directly comparable.
High inference-flip rates indicate sensitivity to specification choices, even though the reported sign-reversal rates are zero.
The evidence is associational; the supplied results do not establish that skin tone causes referee decisions.

sendoff_outcome_definition.label: Definition of a red-card outcome
sendoff_outcome_definition.rationale: Should the outcome be straight red cards only, or all sendings-off including second-yellow cards?  [found by: direct]

straight_red_only.label: Straight red cards only
straight_red_only.description: Define the event count for each player-referee dyad as `redCards`; exclude `yellowReds`.

all_sendings_off.label: Straight red or second-yellow sending-off
all_sendings_off.description: Define the event count as `redCards + yellowReds` for each player-referee dyad.

skin_tone_measurement_and_encoding.label: Measurement and encoding of skin tone
skin_tone_measurement_and_encoding.rationale: How should `rater1` and `rater2` be combined and represented as the exposure?  [found by: direct]

mean_continuous.label: Mean rater score as a continuous predictor
mean_continuous.description: Compute `skin_tone = (rater1 + rater2) / 2` and enter it as a linear predictor ranging from 0 to 1.

mean_five_level_factor.label: Mean score as a five-level factor
mean_five_level_factor.description: Compute `(rater1 + rater2) / 2` and treat the values 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1 as five indicator-coded categories, using 0 as the reference category.

mean_binary_threshold.label: Binary light/dark classification
mean_binary_threshold.description: Compute `(rater1 + rater2) / 2`; classify scores below 0.5 as light and scores greater than or equal to 0.5 as dark, then estimate the dark-versus-light contrast.

rater1_continuous.label: First rater score as a continuous predictor
rater1_continuous.description: Use `rater1` directly as a linear predictor from 0 to 1 and ignore `rater2`.

exposure_and_event_model.label: Model for event counts and game exposure
exposure_and_event_model.rationale: How should the `redCards` or combined sending-off count be related to the number of games in `games`?  [found by: direct]

binomial_count_rate.label: Binomial rate model
binomial_count_rate.description: Use the selected sending-off count as the number of successes and `games` as the number of trials in a binomial regression; report the skin-tone odds ratio.

dyad_any_event_logistic.label: Any-event logistic model
dyad_any_event_logistic.description: Replace the selected sending-off count by an indicator equal to 1 when the dyad has at least one event and 0 otherwise; fit an unweighted logistic regression with one observation per dyad, without using `games` as a denominator.

poisson_exposure_model.label: Count model with game exposure offset
poisson_exposure_model.description: Model the selected sending-off count with Poisson regression and include `log(games)` as an offset, interpreting the skin-tone coefficient as a rate-ratio contrast rather than an odds ratio.

repeated_player_referee_structure.label: Dependence from repeated players and referees
repeated_player_referee_structure.rationale: How should the repeated observations for the same `playerShort` and `refNum` be represented in the model?  [found by: direct]

no_random_effects.label: No player or referee random effects
no_random_effects.description: Fit the selected event model with no random intercept for `playerShort` or `refNum`; any adjustment variables are included only as fixed effects.

player_referee_random_intercepts.label: Random intercepts for player and referee
player_referee_random_intercepts.description: Add independent random intercepts for `playerShort` and `refNum` to the selected regression model, while estimating the fixed effect of skin tone.

referee_random_intercept_only.label: Random intercept for referee only
referee_random_intercept_only.description: Add a random intercept for `refNum` but not for `playerShort`, leaving player characteristics represented only by observed covariates.

fixed_covariate_adjustment.label: Adjustment for observed player, league, and referee characteristics
fixed_covariate_adjustment.rationale: Which variables in addition to skin tone should be included as fixed-effect covariates?  [found by: direct]

unadjusted.label: Skin tone only
unadjusted.description: Include no covariates beyond the selected skin-tone exposure and the selected outcome model.

league_position_adjusted.label: League and position adjusted
league_position_adjusted.description: Include categorical `leagueCountry` and categorical `position` as fixed effects in addition to skin tone.

player_characteristics_adjusted.label: Add player characteristics
player_characteristics_adjusted.description: Include `leagueCountry`, `position`, `height`, `weight`, and birth year extracted from `birthday` as fixed effects in addition to skin tone.

referee_bias_adjusted.label: Add referee-country bias measures
referee_bias_adjusted.description: Include `leagueCountry`, `position`, `height`, `weight`, birth year from `birthday`, `meanIAT`, and `meanExp` as fixed effects in addition to skin tone.

uncertainty_accounting.label: Uncertainty calculation for repeated dyads
uncertainty_accounting.rationale: How should standard errors or confidence intervals account for dependence among rows involving the same players and referees?  [found by: direct]

model_based_uncertainty.label: Model-based standard errors
model_based_uncertainty.description: Use the standard errors and confidence intervals implied by the selected regression model, with no additional clustering or resampling.

two_way_clustered_uncertainty.label: Two-way clustered uncertainty
two_way_clustered_uncertainty.description: Calculate sandwich standard errors clustered simultaneously by `playerShort` and `refNum`, using a multiway-cluster correction for their overlap.

cluster_bootstrap_uncertainty.label: Cluster bootstrap
cluster_bootstrap_uncertainty.description: Resample `playerShort` clusters and `refNum` clusters in a two-way cluster bootstrap, refit the complete model for each replicate, and use the bootstrap distribution for confidence intervals.
